rules.title: Ban on using or distributing a common pricing algorithm as part of a conspiracy in restraint of trade (AB 325)
rules.requirement: A person may not use or distribute a common pricing algorithm (software or other method used by two or more persons that uses competitor data to recommend, set, or influence a price or commercial term) as part of a contract, combination, or conspiracy to restrain trade under the Cartwright Act. This applies generally, including to landlords setting rents.
rules.key_value: Prohibition on use or distribution of a common pricing algorithm in a conspiracy to restrain trade
rules.coverage_conditions: Any person, other than the end consumer, who uses or distributes a common pricing algorithm that uses competitor data. It is not limited to housing, so it covers rental pricing.
rules.exemptions: End consumers are excluded from the definition of 'person'.

coverage.unverifiable_conditions: Requires use of a common pricing algorithm (used by two or more persons and using competitor data) as part of a contract, combination, or conspiracy to restrain trade.

rules.penalty: Cartwright Act enforcement; violations are punishable as a crime.
rules.citation: Cal. Bus. & Prof. Code § 16729(a) (AB 325, Stats. 2025, ch. 338)
rules.quoted_span: (a) It shall be unlawful for a person to use or distribute a common pricing algorithm as part of a contract, combination in the form of a trust, or conspiracy to restrain trade or commerce in violation of this chapter.
rules.conflict_note: The document shows only enactment (approved and chaptered October 6, 2025) with no effective date stated. The effective date of January 1, 2026 is inferred from California's default rule for regular-session statutes. The law is a general antitrust statute rather than housing-specific.

rules.title: Ban on using or distributing a common pricing algorithm while coercing adoption of recommended prices (AB 325)
rules.requirement: A person may not use or distribute a common pricing algorithm if they coerce another person to set or adopt a price or commercial term recommended by the algorithm for the same or similar products or services in California. This applies generally, including to rental housing pricing.
rules.key_value: Prohibition on coercing adoption of algorithm-recommended prices or terms
rules.coverage_conditions: Any person, other than the end consumer, using or distributing a common pricing algorithm who coerces another to adopt its recommended price or commercial term (for example, level of service, availability, or output) for the same or similar products or services in California.
rules.exemptions: End consumers are excluded from the definition of 'person'.

coverage.unverifiable_conditions: Requires coercion of another person to adopt a price or commercial term recommended by a common pricing algorithm.

rules.penalty: Cartwright Act enforcement; violations are punishable as a crime.
rules.citation: Cal. Bus. & Prof. Code § 16729(b) (AB 325, Stats. 2025, ch. 338)
rules.quoted_span: (b) It shall be unlawful for a person to use or distribute a common pricing algorithm if the person coerces another person to set or adopt a recommended price or commercial term recommended by the common pricing algorithm for the same or similar products or services in the jurisdiction of this state.
rules.conflict_note: The document shows only enactment (approved and chaptered October 6, 2025) with no effective date stated. The effective date of January 1, 2026 is inferred from California's default rule for regular-session statutes. The law is a general antitrust statute rather than housing-specific.
